//: The measured cell, the pinned font, the toolchain, and where the design disagrees with the product. Each contradiction is a bug in .claude/design/ or a decision the developer made against it, not a bug in the app; it leaves when the design is fixed upstream or the decision reversed. See crates/review/src/baseline.rs.

contradictions.design_says: Frame `A launch` draws the mark as 18 × 6 cells of `1ch` × `--row` (24px) on a 14px font — an 8.4 × 12px half-cell, so the letter is about as wide as it is tall.
contradictions.design_also_says: A terminal's row is shorter: on the cell `measure` pins (8 × 18) the half-cell is 8 × 9, and the same 18 × 6 cells draw the A a quarter shorter than the frame does, and a third again as wide as it is tall.
contradictions.app_follows: The frame's letter redrawn 7 rows tall on its own 18 columns by the generator (`fit_to_terminal` in `crates/review/src/tokens.rs`): the frame's stroke, its outer edge sampled along 14 half-rows, each half-row the fill of the frame's nearest. At 6 rows the rule gives the frame's cells exactly. The launch card is one row taller. 7 rows, not the 8 that would keep the letter's own proportion, because the frame's facts sit on 24px rows too: at 8 the mark outweighs them, at 7 the letter is a little wide and the balance close to the frame's. Only the mark is redrawn. Retired when the design draws the mark for a terminal's cell.

contradictions.design_says: The glyph table (guidelines/glyphs.html, README's Iconography) contains no box-drawing characters, and nothing inside a window is stroked.
contradictions.design_also_says: The design system has no table component at all — its components are Frame, Field, StatusBar, ContextBar, UserEcho, Prose, Disclosure, PlanStep, Mark, LaunchCard, QuestionPanel, CommandRow and the review set — and a set of flat grounds cannot express a two-dimensional grid of cell boundaries.
contradictions.app_follows: ADR 0002 — a markdown table in assistant prose is drawn with `┌ ┬ ┐ ├ ┼ ┤ └ ┴ ┘ ─ │`, scoped to that one construct. Retired when the design system gains a table component.

contradictions.design_says: Frame `F commands` types `/c` and the list narrows to `changes` and `clear`, with no shortcut column; the design system's `CommandRow` still shows `changes`, `undo` (`↺`) and `quit` (`⌃D`), a key right-flush like a menu.
contradictions.design_also_says: Nothing in the design names `/resume` (ADR 0005, a shipped feature), `/model`, `/connect` (ADR 0012) or `/theme`, and the product has neither `/changes` nor `/undo`.
contradictions.app_follows: The developer's decisions of 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-25: `/resume`, `/model`, `/connect` (ADR 0012, 2026-09-26), `/quit` and `/exit` (one command, both in the list), `/clear` and `/theme`, with no shortcut column — as frame F now draws it. The panel's grid, tones, completion and selection are the frame's exactly; only its rows differ. `/changes` and `/undo` are open-tasks entry 27.

contradictions.design_says: `tokens/layout.css` is the grid, and the app draws every measure through it: `--margin-x`, `--body-x`, `--number-col` and the rest, each a token the frames read with `var(--…)`.
contradictions.design_also_says: Frame E's `QuestionPanel` positions its contents with measures no token names: the panel's text is `padding:0 3ch` inside it, and each option row is `margin:0 1ch` inside the panel.
contradictions.app_follows: Frame E's values, as the named constants `PANEL_PAD` (3) and `OPTION_INSET` (1) in `crates/tui/src/ui/question.rs`, citing this entry. Remove both, and this entry, when `layout.css` names them and the generator carries them.

contradictions.design_says: `tokens/colors.css`: `--label3` is the “tertiary: line numbers, folders, pending” tone — 2.5:1 on `--win` in the dark theme, 2.9:1 in the light — and the caption over the review frames G–J: “⌃↩ stays grey until every file is read, then turns blue.”
contradictions.design_also_says: Apple's HIG (Accessibility): “Strive to meet color contrast minimum standards.” — 4.5:1 for text up to 17 pts — and “Convey information with more than color alone.”
contradictions.app_follows: The design's `label3`, unchanged (the developer's decision, 2026-09-24). The not-ready approve does not rely on colour alone: until every file is read its words say so too, and they change when it is ready.

contradictions.design_says: README: “Comments ride at the end of their line, `◆ Use config`, like an Xcode annotation. The code is never broken up.”
contradictions.design_also_says: Apple's HIG (Layout): “For example, horizontally adjacent views may need to stack vertically to provide more space for text; table rows or other containers may need to grow in height so that text isn’t cropped or doesn’t overlap other content; and table rows with a single line of text by default might need to grow vertically to accommodate multiple lines of text.”
contradictions.app_follows: The HIG (the developer's decision, 2026-09-24): a diff line longer than the pane wraps onto continuation rows with a blank gutter, rather than being cut at the pane's edge.

contradictions.design_says: The design system's components are Frame, Field, StatusBar, ContextBar, UserEcho, Prose, Disclosure, PlanStep, Mark, LaunchCard, QuestionPanel, CommandRow and the review set; none of them connects an account, and no frame shows a code to enter elsewhere.
contradictions.design_also_says: The Content Fundamentals: lead with a sentence, outcomes not tool names. A device-code sign-in is one URL, one code and one outcome.
contradictions.app_follows: ADR 0012 — bare `/connect` is a QuestionPanel listing the accounts ("Which account?", each with the subscription it needs as its fact); the sign-in's prompt ("Open <url> and enter the code <code>. It is good for 30 minutes.") and its outcome ("Connected to x.ai. …") are notices. Retired when the design system draws a connection of its own.
